solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brother knowledgeable about the setter's sort of music

definitions.note: 'Brother!' is an exclamation of surprise, used here as a whole interjection

parts.note: to be well up on a subject is to be knowledgeable about it
on means about, as in a talk on birds
the setter refers to himself, so his is my
soul is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A monk who knows a lot about the kind of music the compiler likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' looks like a monk or sibling but is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of astonishment, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: International organisation split about supplier of mutton that's not fresh

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: the split word goes around the sheep

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart or split
a ewe is a female sheep, whose meat is mutton

explanation.surface: A global body divided over the source of some stale meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not renewed has not been refreshed or replaced, so it is stale or out of date.

clue.text: Work can be engaging

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Work that can be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' looks like charming but means choosing to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose to participate in a scheme is to engage with it rather than stay out.

clue.text: Component of world trade

parts.note: Mercury is a planet, a world
to trade is to swap or switch

explanation.surface: Something forming part of global commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world trade' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical device that uses a blob of liquid metal to make contact, a part of a circuit.

clue.text: Singular tinkles having function in clocks

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: the tinkles word has the function word within it

parts.note: tinkle is a childish word for urinating, as is pee
a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: Odd chiming sounds that are part of how clocks work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clocks' looks like timepieces but means speed dials.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a vehicle's speedometers are called clocks, and this is a short form of the same word.

clue.text: Eco tour might at first be arranged

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new order
the opening letter of might is taken

explanation.surface: An eco-tour that might, initially, be organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eco' suggests green tourism but is the Italian novelist; the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Name of the Rose is known by this forename and that surname.

clue.text: Tip from agent to stay close to violent criminal

indicators.note: a tip is an end point, so the final letter of agent is taken

parts.note: to hug something is to keep close to it, as a ship hugs the coast

explanation.surface: Advice from a secret agent about keeping near a dangerous offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice but means the end of the word agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a ruffian who uses brutal force in committing crimes.

clue.text: Briefly shed remaining shift towards nine o'clock?

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a hangar is a large shed for aircraft
what is left is remaining

explanation.surface: Quickly losing what was left of one's working shift towards the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: On a clock face nine o'clock points left, so this is to turn left.
explanation.definitionFit: An American idiom for turning to the left, the direction the hour hand points at nine.

clue.text: Group equipped to breathe in water through the mouth

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word passes through the speaker's mouth

parts.note: a fish that has gills is gilled

explanation.surface: A school of fish that can take in water through their mouths.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures fish, which do draw water in by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An association of craftsmen or merchants is a group of people with a shared trade.

clue.text: Pensioner, perhaps, on Hebridean island

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a business letter
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: An elderly person drawing a pension living on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working is usually drawing a pension; 'perhaps' because not every one does.

clue.text: Root, at first needing juice, in rare source of bark

parts.note: a root is a base or foundation

indicators.note: the opening letters of needing, juice and in are taken

explanation.surface: A plant root that needs moisture, found inside an unusual kind of tree bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' suggests a tree, with root and juice backing that up; it is a dog's bark.
explanation.definitionFit: This African hunting dog is famously almost barkless, yodelling instead, so it rarely produces a bark.

clue.text: Pretty individual standing in street — opposite side

parts.note: a sub, or substitute, is a person standing in for another
anti means opposed
an ally is someone on your side

explanation.surface: An attractive person waiting in the road on the far side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like attractive but is an adverb meaning considerably.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean to a large degree, as in fairly or considerably different.

clue.text: One ostrich-like Greek character crossing sand, concealing head

indicators.note: the Greek letter spans across the remaining sand letters, holding them inside

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the head of sand, its first letter, is hidden away and lost

explanation.surface: An ostrich-like bird, Greek in character, crossing the sand with its head buried.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the myth of ostriches burying their heads in sand.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for the rhea, a large flightless South American bird resembling an ostrich.

clue.text: Rush to get on, achieving target

parts.note: to dart is to dash or rush
to board a bus or train is to get on it

explanation.surface: Hurrying to catch a train and achieving one's aim.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the players aim at this circular target hung on a wall.

clue.text: Dispersing sin abroad — why the just prevail

indicators.note: scattering the letters of these words before reassembling them

explanation.surface: Spreading sin around the world: why do the righteous triumph?
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like the righteous but means barely; 'abroad' is fodder, not a second signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from horse racing: to triumph by the narrowest margin, barely prevailing.

clue.text: Mean to collect tax once monthly — ultimately vital

indicators.note: the mean word gathers the tax inside itself

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean
cess was a historical local tax

indicators.note: the last letter of monthly is taken

explanation.surface: A miser collecting a monthly tax, which is finally essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an average but is a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something essential that cannot be done without.

clue.text: Rows we hear with visitors on doorstep?

definitions.meaning: rows are noisy quarrels or arguments

definitions.text: we hear with visitors on doorstep?
definitions.meaning: the two-tone chime of a doorbell rung by callers

explanation.surface: Quarrels heard when guests stand at the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British for heated arguments, and the sound of the bell when someone calls.

clue.text: Legendary Englishman busy making lots of runs, keeping wicket

indicators.note: the words hold the wicket letter within them

parts.note: busy is slang for a detective, as is dick
a batsman who scores a century is hitting a ton
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A legendary English cricketer scoring heavily while also acting as wicketkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton is a century (100 runs) in cricket; 'keeping' slips the wicket letter in after the detective word, not round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk hero who walked to London with his cat and became Lord Mayor, famous from pantomime.

clue.text: Border, not left bolted down: thereby flatter?

indicators.note: the left letter, L, is dropped

parts.note: a limit is a border or boundary
to bolt food is to eat it quickly, so ate

explanation.surface: A border bolted down rather than to the left, as a way of flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: Imitation is said to be the sincerest form of flattery, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying someone is a way of praising them, as the proverb about the sincerest form of flattery says.

clue.text: Sometimes on, sometimes off, like a duffel coat?

definitions.meaning: a switch flipped between two states
a duffel coat is fastened with wooden pegs on loops

explanation.surface: A coat that is worn some days and not others.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched back and forth between two states, and fitted with the pegs a duffel coat closes with.

clue.text: Large bats that sing at day's end?

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Big bats that sing at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but is an adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the final act before bed, done at the close of the day.

clue.text: Form of gambling not tolerated after shrinking returns

indicators.note: the inner run is then turned round
the phrase is shrunk at both ends so only an inner run remains

explanation.surface: A kind of betting banned after a decline in profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like winnings but signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance drawing numbers for prizes, a lottery or bingo-like game.

clue.text: Shooting home to meet friend

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: Firing a gun at home to meet a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' looks like gunfire but means a plant putting out shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is coming into leaf, putting out new growth, is said to be in this state.

clue.text: Russian cakes and odd helpings of Belgian pie

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on, are served up

explanation.surface: Russian pastries alongside an odd Belgian pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Small buckwheat pancakes from Russia, often served with caviar and sour cream.

clue.text: What to carry back with a vital pipe

indicators.note: the two words are read backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what was said
to cart something is to carry it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about taking an essential pipe home.
explanation.definitionFit: This airway tube carries air to the lungs, so it is a pipe one cannot live without.

clue.text: Female climber's unending stocking trouble

indicators.note: to stock is to hold within, so the shortened plant keeps the trouble inside
the end letter is taken off

parts.note: a liana is a climbing woody vine of tropical forests
ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: A woman climber's endless trouble with her stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so the clue's female stands for her.

clue.text: Stone axes: small number returned

indicators.note: the letters are sent back, read right to left

parts.note: the axes of a graph are labelled x and y
no is the abbreviation for number, and small means abbreviated

explanation.surface: Stone axes from prehistory, a few of them brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like tools but means graph axes.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony quartz, used as a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Different MPs readily listen to me

indicators.note: the letters are made different, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Various members of parliament eagerly asking for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic catchphrase demanding attention, famous from George Bush's no-new-taxes pledge.
